sentences.text: There’s one more vessel to place, and she only exists offshore.
Constrained by her draft is International only.
You won’t find her in the Inland rules.

Under the International rules, any vessel other than one not under command, or one restricted in her ability to maneuver, shall, if the circumstances allow, avoid impeding the safe passage of a vessel constrained by her draft.
That’s a deep ship in a channel she can’t leave, showing the signals of Rule twenty-eight.
In return, the constrained vessel has a duty of her own.
She navigates with particular caution, with full regard to her special condition.
Now notice the words avoid impeding.
Remember from Rule eight what that means?
It means acting early to leave her sea room.
It isn’t the same thing as give-way and stand-on.
So if an exam question asks who is the stand-on vessel here, be careful.
The rule doesn’t use those words.
